title: AMD Stock Faces $500 Support as Big Tech and Intel Earnings Shake Semiconductor Rally
summary: AMD Stock Faces $500 Support as Big Tech and Intel Earnings Shake Semiconductor Rally
detailed: AMD stock reversed on Friday, falling toward $500 after disappointing earnings from Amazon and Intel intensified concerns about AI infrastructure spending, semiconductor valuations and the sustainability of the technology rally.
The stock fell toward $527 in after-hours trading as disappointing results from Intel and Amazon weakened sentiment across the technology sector.

Intel’s latest earnings highlighted progress in its 18A manufacturing technology and data-centre business, but weakness in the PC market and continued manufacturing losses remain significant challenges.
For now, concerns about financing, elevated valuations and disappointing big-tech earnings are challenging the semiconductor rally, leaving AMD vulnerable to further volatility.
sentences: AMD stock reversed on Friday, falling toward $500 after disappointing earnings from Amazon and Intel intensified concerns about AI infrastructure spending, semiconductor valuations and the sustainability of the technology rally.
Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) shares came under renewed selling pressure on Friday after recovering earlier in the week.
The stock fell toward $527 in after-hours trading as disappointing results from Intel and Amazon weakened sentiment across the technology sector.
The sell-off follows concerns over capital expenditure from Google and Microsoft, raising questions about whether massive infrastructure investments can generate sufficient returns.
Investors are increasingly scrutinising semiconductor valuations as spending commitments rise and expectations remain elevated.

Intel’s latest earnings highlighted progress in its 18A manufacturing technology and data-centre business, but weakness in the PC market and continued manufacturing losses remain significant challenges.
The results failed to reassure investors, sending Intel shares lower.
Amazon also disappointed, reporting third-quarter earnings of $1.89 per share against expectations of $1.96.
Revenue reached $201.9 billion, narrowly missing the $202.1 billion consensus estimate.
Amazon’s shares fell toward $220, extending losses after the report.
Its fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $240 billion to $247 billion, compared with expectations of $244.3 billion, added to uncertainty across the technology sector.
Although neither company’s results directly determine AMD’s performance, their impact on investor confidence has contributed to broader selling in semiconductor and growth stocks.
A report from Seoul’s Maeil Business Newspaper said Nvidia and Tesla planned to invest $2.8 billion in Samsung Electro-Mechanics to build chip-substrate factories.
The reported investment has raised questions about circular financing, in which companies provide capital to partners or customers that subsequently purchase their products.
Such arrangements can support supply-chain expansion, but investors may question whether reported demand reflects independent spending or relies partly on financing from industry participants.

As semiconductor companies commit billions to manufacturing capacity and data-centre infrastructure, investors are becoming more sensitive to funding requirements and the financial sustainability of expansion plans.
Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) shares fell around 8%, threatening to break below $500 after reaching a record above $658.
The reversal reflects broader weakness across semiconductor stocks, as investors reassess valuations and the financial commitments required to expand computing infrastructure.
ASML reported record third-quarter sales of €11.7 billion and forecast fourth-quarter revenue of €14.2 billion to €15.2 billion.
However, its narrowed 2026 sales guidance of €44 billion to €45 billion and warnings about manufacturing capacity highlighted challenges facing the semiconductor industry.
The company expects planned capacity in 2027 and 2028 to fall short of anticipated demand.
Although supply constraints could support pricing, they also underline the substantial investment required to expand production.
ASML shares fell approximately 4% in overnight trading, adding further pressure to semiconductor sentiment.
Despite the recent weakness, AMD retains significant long-term growth opportunities.
Citi analyst Atif Malik believes personal computing agents could increase demand for central processing units, potentially benefiting AMD and Intel.
Meta Platforms, a major AMD server customer, could provide additional demand as its computing requirements expand.
AMD estimates its addressable market across GPUs, server CPUs and data-centre infrastructure could reach approximately $2 trillion by 2030.
The company also expects its data-centre business to double in 2027, reaching approximately $70 billion in sales.
However, achieving that target will require sustained demand and successful execution.
AMD’s decision to back a $300 million loan for infrastructure startup Crusoe adds another financial commitment tied to data-centre expansion, reinforcing the importance of funding conditions.
AMD’s retreat toward $527 puts the psychological $500 level in focus.
A sustained break below this threshold could intensify selling, particularly if weakness spreads across semiconductor stocks and investors reduce exposure to high-growth technology companies.
Conversely, a recovery above $550 could help stabilise the short-term outlook.
However, AMD’s ability to regain momentum will depend on whether investors remain confident in future data-centre demand and the returns from infrastructure spending.
For now, concerns about financing, elevated valuations and disappointing big-tech earnings are challenging the semiconductor rally, leaving AMD vulnerable to further volatility.
